concern: Verify interactive touch target bounding boxes consistently satisfy 44x44px minimums across mobile viewport layouts.
jtbd: When interacting with UI controls on mobile viewports, I want clickable and tappable elements to have a physical bounding box of at least 44x44px, so that I can reliably activate targets without accidental misclicks or motor strain.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a mobile viewport layout width of 375px to 428px, When evaluating the bounding box dimensions of all interactive elements (buttons, navigation links, icon controls, and form inputs), Then each element's touch target area spans at least 44x44 CSS pixels with sufficient clearance from adjacent interactive targets.
editInstruction: On mobile viewport layouts (<768px), adjust interactive components (action buttons, icon triggers, and navigation pills) so their touch target bounding areas satisfy min-width: 44px and min-height: 44px (using touch target padding where visible dimensions are smaller), maintaining optical balance and avoiding overlap.

concern: Monitor subtle metadata and muted badge text elements for WCAG AA 4.5:1 contrast compliance across alternative theme variants.
jtbd: When viewing secondary metadata and muted status badges across light and dark theme variations, I want text foreground colors to maintain sufficient luminance contrast against badge backgrounds, so that secondary information remains effortlessly legible without eye strain.
acceptanceCriteria: Given any supported theme variant (light, dark, high contrast), When measuring color luminance contrast between metadata/badge text and its immediate background surface, Then the contrast ratio is at least 4.5:1 for regular text and at least 3.0:1 for bold/large text according to WCAG 2.1 AA specifications.
editInstruction: Audit and adjust the color token assignments for muted badge backgrounds and subtle metadata labels across all theme variants so that foreground text achieves a minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio against badge container surfaces while retaining secondary visual hierarchy.
